task.description: WF-02, step 1b, pass 3 of 3 — the LAST allowed pass of the gate CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on the design of REQ-105 (docs/design/REQ-105-e2e-picker.md). Pass 1 (N1-N11) and pass 2 (N12-N17) were FAIL; step 01e claims N12-N17 closed and a sweep of the same kind of mistake over the whole design (table 14.1 'test x first sub-step', the waits written down, recounted figures F42). Do the whole gate again by the section "Step 1b" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md; read the design and the block REQ-105 yourself. Repeat on a fresh clone of the tag base/E2E105-20261105-01 (outside the project; the design and decision 0109 are not in the tag): (a) N12 — apply the sub-steps in order on a copy and run every test the design lists for each state; the state of table 14.1 must match what you measure, row by row, for at least the states after sub-steps 1-2, 3 and 4a; (b) N13 — build the stand-in with-child mode, the starter and E2S-13 from the TEXT ONLY and apply mutant S02; also confirm the order 'ready event, then link' needs no sleep; (c) the new mutants S20, S21, P22, P23 and the ones you could not kill before (Q15, S19 are declared informational/equivalent; S22 declared not testable by decision 0109 O13 — judge whether that declaration is honest); (d) at least 10 more mutants of your own, including against the real page; (e) re-measure  three times. Judge strictly but only on what the gate checks; a remark that is a wish, not a gap, is Low and does not fail the pass. If you find a Medium or High gap, FAIL with concrete one-sentence fixes. Task text and report hold no absolute machine paths and no names of other projects of the owner (not even as examples). End every process you start by explicit pid and check with ps at the end.

Verdict PASS or FAIL with concrete remarks

findings.place: section 16, row S19 and the header list 'Survivors and informational cases' (1); 4.1 stop(); 4.3 mode with-child
findings.what: S19 (SIGTERM to the leader only, then the final SIGKILL to the group) is declared 'applied, survives, equivalent: the effect is the same'. It is not the same: when the child of with-child logs a line in its SIGTERM handler, the log has that line in 5 of 5 stops with the group signal and in 0 of 5 with SIGTERM to the leader only. The contract 'stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group' is in 4.1 and in the README text of section 10, and no starter test holds it.
findings.needed: Either let the SIGTERM handler of the --child process append one event (for example child-term) to the log and let E2S-13 hold that event for the child's pid after stop() (then S19 is caught), or move S19 from 'equivalent' to 'survivor on record: group SIGTERM is not tested'. Do not call it equivalent.

findings.pass_item: B5, Q5 (failure path with a state check)
findings.place: section 4.1 step 3 ('A throw or an error event'), section 5 row 3, E2S-02/03/04
findings.what: The path 'spawn throws at once' (not the error event) has a rule (STAND_START_FAILED, marker removed) but no test: my mutant T06 (marker left after a synchronous throw) survives all 20 starter tests. E2S-04 covers only the error-event path (missing cwd); E2S-02/03 use a deps.spawn that throws but only to count calls.
findings.needed: Name one more case in E2S-04 or E2S-02: a deps.spawn that throws -> STAND_START_FAILED, no sai-e2e-* folder, nothing registered. Or write T06 into section 16 as a survivor on record.

findings.what: The tail of the message STAND_EXIT is stated ('after SIGTERM' or 'on its own') but only the second wording is asserted (E2S-11); a stop() that always says 'on its own' (my T05) survives. Also a stop() that does not wait for the group to be gone (T02) survives, because the tests poll with waitGone as AP-144 demands - that one is informational.
findings.needed: E2S-09 may assert the words 'after SIGTERM' in the message. T02 needs nothing.

For DOC-UPDATER (Q13) from this gate: (a) a mutant called equivalent must be tried with a stand-in that can show the difference (S19 was called equivalent without a child that logs the signal); (b) a no-op mutant (a weaker CSS selector than the page's own, M16 first form) proves nothing - check that the mutant changes the measured value before reading the result; (c) a harness that kills leftovers by the path of the copy misses processes started with a relative path (the leaked picker of T01): look for leftovers by the program name (LEFT of section 16).

Not a finding of the design: my own test file for the starter has five empty catch blocks that eslint rejects; it was a throw-away copy outside the project. BACKEND-DEV and TEST-DESIGNER run lint on theirs.
